lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello, yes I do! I have a son, Alex, who's 16. I'm living here in the UK and he lives at home with me. I was wondering if I could claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions:

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? For example, is he enrolled in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or similar qualifications) or an approved training program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Since Alex is 16 and studying A-levels, that would typically count as approved education.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to ask: Are you the person primarily responsible for Alex? This means you live with him and are responsible for his day-to-day care and upbringing?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. He lives at home with me and I'm responsible for looking after him day-to-day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

Do you currently live in the UK, and are you a UK resident for tax purposes? Or if not, do you have any circumstances that might affect your residency status (such as recently moving to or from the UK)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're based in Manchester, so no issues there with residency.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you. Just one more important question:

Is there anyone else who also has a child living with them and who might be claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or are you the only person claiming for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's just me - nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:
- Alex is 16 and studying A-levels at sixth form college, which qualifies as approved full-time education
- You live in the UK and are responsible for Alex's day-to-day care
- Alex lives at home with you
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit. You can claim Child Benefit for Alex while he continues in approved education or training, which can extend until he turns 20 (as long as he remains in qualifying education that started before his 20th birthday).

To make your claim, you can apply online through the government website or by post. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
